title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
summary: On 10 December 1948 the UN General Assembly, meeting in Paris, adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights by a vote of 48 to none with 8 abstentions. Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the drafting committee. It set out rights to which all people are entitled and became a reference point for later human rights law.

uncertainty.note: The date and tally agree across pages. The Third Committee had earlier approved the text 29 to none with 7 abstentions; that is a separate vote.

as_recorded.value: forty-eight to zero with eight abstentions

where.historical_name: Palais de Chaillot, Paris, France (seat of the UN General Assembly's 1948 session)

importance.justification: The first global statement of universal human rights, it underpins international human rights law.

related.because: South Africa, which began apartheid legislation that year, abstained from the vote.
